title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
summary: Tense and relax each muscle group: to tighten, to stretch.
script:
Hello, and welcome. This is your moment, a small space carved out just for you, in the middle of everything else.

Take a little time to settle into a position that feels right. Sitting, lying down, whatever your body prefers today. There's no correct way to begin, only the way that feels natural to you.

Let your eyes close softly, like a door closing quietly at the end of the day. Or if you'd rather, let them rest, unfocused, looking gently downward.

For these next few minutes, there's nothing else you need to attend to. Just this. Just you, and this quiet space you've made.

Feel the surface beneath you, holding your weight completely. Notice your body settling, becoming a little heavier, a little more still.

Take a slow breath in… and let it out.

Once more. In… and out.

Today, we're going to move slowly through the body, using two simple movements. Movements your body already knows well, even without thinking about them.

The first is to tighten. To tighten means to make something tighter or more secure, like when we tighten our seatbelt on a plane.

The second is to stretch. To stretch means to pull something so it becomes longer, like when you stretch your arms after sitting for a long time.

We'll move through the body, tightening one part, and then stretching it. Tighten… and stretch. There's no rush here. Each part deserves a little time, a little attention.

Let's begin with your hands. Tighten them now, closing them slowly into soft fists. Feel the tightening in your fingers, your knuckles, your palms.

Hold this for a moment.

Now stretch. Open your hands completely, spreading your fingers as far as they'll go, reaching outward, lengthening every part.

Notice the difference between these two feelings. The tightening, close and firm. The stretch, open and long.

Let your hands rest now, somewhere between the two, soft and comfortable.

Move to your arms. Tighten them, bending your elbows, pulling your hands in towards your shoulders, making everything firm and close.

Hold this tightening for a moment.

Now stretch. Slowly extend your arms outward, reaching as far as feels comfortable, lengthening from your shoulders all the way to your fingertips.

Notice this stretch settling into your muscles, gentle and satisfying.

Let your arms rest now, resting wherever feels natural.

Bring your attention to your shoulders. Tighten them, lifting them up towards your ears, pulling them inward and close.

Hold this for a moment.

Now stretch. Let your shoulders roll gently back down, opening your chest, lengthening the space across your collarbone.

Feel this openness settling in, wide and easy.

Move to your back. Tighten it slightly, pulling your shoulder blades together, making the muscles firm.

Hold this tightening.

Now stretch. Let your back lengthen, imagining space growing between each part of your spine, from your neck all the way down.

Notice your back feeling longer now, more open, more spacious.

Bring your attention to your legs. Tighten them, pointing your toes, making the muscles firm from your thighs down to your feet.

Hold this for a moment.

Now stretch. Let your legs lengthen, reaching gently outward, as if trying to touch something far away, without any strain.

Feel this stretch settling into your legs, long and comfortable.

Finally, tighten your whole body, all at once. Every part, drawn inward, firm and close together, just for a moment.

And now, stretch everything outward. Let your arms reach. Let your legs lengthen. Let your whole body open, as wide and as long as it comfortably can.

Notice this feeling spreading through you, this sense of openness, of space, of length.

Let your body rest now, settling naturally, somewhere between tight and stretched, in a place that feels balanced and calm.

There's something worth noticing here. Your body moves naturally between these two states, tightening, and stretching, all day long, usually without your awareness. Today, you've simply paid attention.

Stay here for a while, feeling this balance. Not tight. Not overly stretched. Simply comfortable, simply at ease.

Let these gentle words settle into your mind.

My body knows how to tighten, and how to stretch.

I can find balance between the two.

I am open.

I am calm.

I am completely at rest.

Take another slow breath, and let these words settle a little deeper.

For a while longer, just stay here. There's no rush to move, no need to do anything at all. Let your body remain exactly as it is, soft, long, and calm.

Notice how peaceful it feels to simply exist in this balanced state, neither pulling inward, nor reaching outward. Just present, just still.

When your mind feels ready, begin to notice small things around you. The temperature of the air. Any distant sounds. Your breath, still slow, and steady.

Let your fingers move first, just slightly. Then let your body take one long, gentle stretch, whatever feels natural, whatever your body wants in this moment.

Take your time returning. There's no hurry.

Whenever you're ready, let your eyes open softly, taking in the light around you.

Carry this awareness with you. Notice, throughout your day, the small moments when your body tightens, and the moments when it stretches and releases. Both are natural. Both have their place.

You are calm. You are balanced. And you are exactly where you need to be.
